html:
An English mathematician who laid the foundations of computer science and helped break German codes in the Second World War. He lived from 1912 to 1954.

In 1936 he described an imaginary machine that reads and writes symbols on a tape, following simple rules. He showed that one such machine could do the work of any other, the idea of the universal computer, and that some problems can never be solved by any machine.

In the war he worked at Bletchley Park, the British code breaking centre. He led the attack on the German naval Enigma code and designed the Bombe, an electromechanical machine that searched for each day's settings. Breaking these codes helped the Allies win the battle against U-boats in the Atlantic.

After the war he designed early electronic computers and in 1950 asked whether machines can think, proposing what is now called the Turing test for artificial intelligence. He also studied how patterns form in living things.

In 1952 he was convicted for a sexual relationship with a man, then a crime in Britain, and forced to take hormone treatment. He died of cyanide poisoning in 1954. Britain apologised in 2009 and pardoned him in 2013.
sum: An English mathematician who laid the foundations of computer science and helped break German codes in the Second World War. He lived from 1912 to 1954.
